LateFeeCalculator unit tests

Save the production class in late_fee_calculator.py, then save the following as test_late_fee_calculator.py. These tests exercise all meaningful decision branches, including weekends, grace-period boundaries, minimum fees, maximum fees, rounding, and non-positive balances.

from datetime import date

import pytest

from late_fee_calculator import LateFeeCalculator


def test_weekday_days_between_returns_zero_for_equal_or_reversed_dates():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator()

    assert calculator._weekday_days_between(date(2026, 1, 5), date(2026, 1, 5)) == 0
    assert calculator._weekday_days_between(date(2026, 1, 6), date(2026, 1, 5)) == 0


def test_weekday_days_between_counts_weekdays_and_skips_weekends():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator()

    # Friday through the following Tuesday: Fri, Mon, Tue
    assert calculator._weekday_days_between(date(2026, 1, 2), date(2026, 1, 6)) == 2


@pytest.mark.parametrize("balance_cents", [0, -1, -10_000])
def test_non_positive_balance_has_no_fee_regardless_of_dates(balance_cents):
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 2, 1))

    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(balance_cents, date(2020, 1, 1)) == 0


def test_fee_is_zero_when_due_date_is_today_or_in_the_future():
    today = date(2026, 1, 12)
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=today)

    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(10_000, today) == 0
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(10_000, date(2026, 1, 13)) == 0


def test_fee_is_zero_at_end_of_ten_weekday_grace_days():
    # Jan 5 through Jan 19 contains exactly 10 weekdays.
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 1, 19))

    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(10_000, date(2026, 1, 5)) == 0


def test_minimum_fee_applies_once_past_grace_period():
    # Jan 5 through Jan 20 contains 11 weekdays, so 1 billable day.
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 1, 20))

    # Raw fee = 10,000 * 0.015 / 30 * 1 = 5 cents; minimum is $5.
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(10_000, date(2026, 1, 5)) == 500


def test_fee_rounds_half_up_before_minimum_or_cap():
    # 11 weekdays past due means one billable day.
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 1, 20))

    # Raw fee = 1,000,000 * 0.015 / 30 = 500.0 cents.
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(1_000_000, date(2026, 1, 5)) == 500

    # Two billable days: raw fee = 1,000,000 * 0.015 / 30 * 2 = 1000 cents.
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 1, 21))
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(1_000_000, date(2026, 1, 5)) == 1000


def test_fee_is_capped_at_twenty_five_percent_of_balance():
    # Enough elapsed weekdays to make the uncapped fee exceed 25%.
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2030, 1, 1))

    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(100_000, date(2026, 1, 5)) == 25_000


def test_weekends_do_not_advance_grace_period():
    # Jan 5 to Jan 19 spans 14 calendar days but only 10 weekdays.
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2026, 1, 19))

    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(50_000, date(2026, 1, 5)) == 0
